chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding the blood-money (diyah) of the slain: 'The heirs inherit it according to the Book of Allah and their shares, if there is no debt upon the slain, except that the brothers and sisters from the mother do not inherit anything from his blood-money.'

key_terms.اَلْإِخْوَةَ وَ اَلْأَخَوَاتِ مِنَ اَلْأ: Brothers and sisters from the mother (maternal siblings)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the blood-money of a deceased person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific application of Quranic inheritance shares to blood-money (diyah), emphasizing that it is treated as an estate distributed among heirs unless debts exist. It notably excludes maternal siblings (al-ikhwah wa al-akhawat min al-umm) from inhering, a ruling that highlights the distinct legal status of maternal kin in Shia jurisprudence compared to their share in the general estate. This ruling is attributed to the practice of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (AS), grounding the legal principle in the Prophet's household's authoritative interpretation.
